  "text": "When the laundrette changed owners, someone removed the chair beside the dryers.

Mr Bell stood in its empty place with his washing bag between his shoes.

“You can leave it running,” the new owner said. “Forty minutes, usually.”

“I know.”

She was kneeling behind the counter, sorting keys into a biscuit tin. Her name was Leila, according to the certificate taped to the wall.

The following Thursday, he brought a folding stool.

Leila said nothing. She had three leaking machines and a card reader that accepted payment only when held at an angle.

By December, Mr Bell had begun bringing two cups of tea from the café next door.

“You don’t have to do that,” she told him.

“They make the second one too weak anyway.”

One morning, he missed his usual time. At noon, Leila found herself looking through the steamed window.

He came the next week with a young woman who carried his bag.

“My daughter,” he said. “She thinks I should get a machine.”

“It would be easier,” his daughter said.

Mr Bell studied the row of turning windows.

Leila fetched the folding stool from behind the counter. She had kept it there since he left it in November.

“We’ve ordered a bench,” she said.

His daughter checked her phone, then put it away.

“Is there a café nearby?”

“Next door,” said Mr Bell. “Don’t ask for a pot. They give you too much water.”

After she went out, he lowered himself onto the stool.

“A bench?”

“Arrives Monday.”

He nodded and began separating his pale shirts from the dark ones."
